topics.topic: Exact owner-session cookie scope, transport, and cross-site policy
questions: Is the owner-session cookie always Secure, or may a local HTTP owner interface receive it?
What exact cookie scope and attributes implement “only to Registry's own origin,” given that cookies are scoped by host/domain and path rather than by full origin or port?
What exact host/domain, path, Secure and SameSite behavior enforces “only to Registry's own origin,” including local HTTP access and cross-site requests?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged question about exact owner-session cookie attributes, scope and cross-site transport policy.

precedent.topic: Owner-session cookie attributes and same-site transport policy
quotes: The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin.
precedent.why: Exact cookie attributes, host/path scope and SameSite transport policy are HTTP contract and encoding details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Exact versioned security-review catalogue and completion criteria
questions: What exact questions and completion criteria define each security-review category for agents working from these texts alone?
What exact questions and completion criteria must later reviewers and implementers apply when that external document is not part of the accepted texts?
What exact, versioned category questions must later reviewers and release checks use to verify that A21 is complete and determine when it must be reopened?

quotes:
The categories are the nine of the Workbench's security review
   (`skills/spec-authoring/SECURITY_REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md`), the catalogue every
   case is reviewed against; this review is complete for that catalogue and
   claims nothing beyond it. That document states the questions each category
   asks; each outcome below answers them by naming the decisions that do, or,
   for NOT_APPLICABLE, why the category's subject is absent.
A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
judgement.divergence: One reviewer treats the nine named outcomes and references as sufficient for completion, while another applies additional or changed questions from an external catalogue; the owner and release reviewers notice different completion and reopening decisions.
judgement.why: State 2 declares the review complete but does not fix within the accepted texts the category questions against which that claim is judged.

topics.topic: Required authenticated backup encryption format and tamper detection
questions: What exact cryptographic backup format makes encryption, tamper detection and later decryption verifiable?
Which authenticated-encryption construction, nonce handling, file format, key identifier and tamper-detection rules must implementations use?
What encryption and authentication format must every release use, and how does restore select the old key after rotation?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about the authenticated backup encryption scheme, key identification and backup metadata format.

precedent.topic: Authenticated backup encryption scheme and metadata format
quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: How imported project display names and aliases are chosen
questions: For each picked project, what determines its imported display name and is an explicit replacement name mandatory?
For each picked project, must the owner explicitly supply a nonblank display name, when may the source name be retained, and is an omitted alias cleared or copied from the source?

quotes:
As the owner picks projects,
   the mapping shows for the picks only: their rooms and pointers; the display
   name and alias each will arrive under (R0-85); the Customers the import
   will make — one for each distinct v1 `customer_ref` a picked project names,
   which is all the file says of a customer (State 1 M04) — with the projects
   each will link (R0-80); and every malformed record and every id that
   conflicts with one production holds.

When the owner picks the projects to import, the owner may give each a new
display name and an alias (R0-82); the project arrives under them, its id kept.

Projects imported
under a person's name (R0-79) are renamed by the owner after the import.

Narrowed by R0-85: they are renamed in the import itself, which also reaches
archived projects.

A required value given as an empty string or as white space only is missing,
   and the action is refused as for a missing value: a project's display name
   and its object's address (R0-45), a Customer's name and kind (Primary
   actions), a room's name (R0-10), a session's access request text.
An optional value given as an empty string or white space only is absent.
judgement.divergence: One implementation requires the owner to supply a nonblank replacement display name and treats an omitted alias as absent, while another retains source values unless replacements are supplied; the owner and every reader of the imported project notice the resulting name and alias or a refused confirmation.
judgement.why: The texts require person-named projects to be renamed during import but do not state the default or mandatory input rule for every picked project's display name and alias.

topics.topic: Multiplicity and replacement or termination semantics of owner sessions
questions: May several owner sessions exist at once, and if so does a new sign-in leave earlier sessions valid or end them?
May several owner sessions exist simultaneously, does a successful sign-in replace earlier sessions, and does sign-out end only the presenting session or all of them?

quotes:
Substitution: two sign-ins are two sessions, each ending on its own; a CSRF
protection is bound to one (R0-29).

The session ends at the first of: 8 hours after sign-in; 30 minutes without
   an owner request; the owner's sign-out; the instance's restart (M11 is never
   durable).
judgement.why: Two sign-ins create distinct concurrently possible sessions, and each session—including the one presented for sign-out—ends on its own.

topics.topic: Pointers of removed artifact types included in the agent projection
questions: Which pointers of a removed type appear in the agent projection?
After a type is removed, does the agent projection carry only its still-published pointer or every retained pointer of that removed type?

quotes:
A release that removes a type keeps every pointer of it, with its status as
   it was: 'list artifacts' and the agent projection still carry them.

The agent projection: `project_id`, alias, status, rooms, and the project's
  current pointers — those `published`, without the superseded and withdrawn
  history, which the owner and the services read (R0-43's minimal projection;
  owner, 2026-10-31; codex round-02 T7) — nothing held as `personal_data`
  (R0-43, R0-68, R0-82).
judgement.why: One passage says the agent projection continues to carry every retained pointer of a removed type, while the other limits that projection to published pointers and excludes superseded and withdrawn history.

topics.topic: Required replay and completion of post-backup privacy state after restore
questions: What prevents Registry from serving after restore before the owner has replayed those changes, and how is completion established?
If a post-backup restriction was later lifted, or an ended relationship was later resumed, what state must the owner re-establish after restore?

quotes:
Restoring production replaces the store with a backup, by the owner on the
   host while Registry is stopped (Explicit exclusions). Every change after the
   backup's instant is lost, the audit entries with it: numbering continues
   from the backup's last number, and the lost entries exist nowhere.

Before
   any service or agent uses the restored instance again the owner repeats,
   in the owner interface, every erasure, restriction and end of a
   relationship made after the backup, from the owner's own record of the
   retention review (R0-60); Registry, which no longer holds them, cannot list
   them.

A Customer's last-changed instant moves by: a correction of its contact,
  kind or fiscal data; restricting and lifting; ending and resuming the
  relationship; erasure.
judgement.divergence: One installation blocks all service and agent use until an explicit replay-complete condition and reconstructs the final privacy state including lifts and resumptions, while another relies only on the owner's procedure and replays the three named change kinds; services, agents, customers and the owner notice different availability and customer restriction or relationship states.
judgement.why: The restore rule requires replay before use but defines neither an enforceable completion condition nor how later inverse transitions affect the state to be restored.

topics.topic: Required status history for imported pointer versions
questions: What exact status pattern must imported versions 1..n have?
For each imported project and type with pointers, must exactly one pointer be `published` and must it be the highest version?

quotes:
A brought-in record is malformed when: a required value is missing (A02);
   it names a project or room the file does not hold; an id occurs
   twice among the file's records of one kind; a status is outside its
   vocabulary, or a pointer is `withdrawn` (v1 never withdrew one, M05); a
   pointer's type is not declared or its owner service is not the type's
   (A22); the versions of a project's pointers of one type are not 1..n, or
   more than one of them is `published`, or a `superseded` one is not lower
   than a later version; an instant cannot be read; an `active` project has an
   archived instant or an `archived` one has none; a `superseded` pointer has
   no superseded instant or a `published` one has one; a record was changed,
   archived or superseded before it was created, added or published.

A pointer the import brings in (R0-50) was published before Registry recorded
principals: the v1 Registry keeps no publisher (its `owner_service` is the
caller's own claim, checked by no token) and no withdrawal (L22).
At every moment a project has at most one `published` pointer of a type.

Publishing a pointer assigns its version, marks the type's published
   pointer `superseded` with its instant, and stores the new pointer
   `published` — all in one transaction, or none of it (R0-17, R0-35).
judgement.divergence: One importer accepts a gap-free history with no published pointer or with a published version below a newer superseded version, while another requires versions 1 through n-1 to be superseded and version n to be the sole published pointer; the owner notices whether the import succeeds and callers notice whether a latest artifact exists.
judgement.why: The malformed-record rules impose only partial status constraints and do not state the complete allowed status pattern for imported version histories.

topics.topic: Restoring older backups across encryption-key and release changes
questions: How is the key for an older backup provided and verified during restore?
Which release must perform a restore, and how is an older backup migrated to the current store version?
How does the restore operation select and receive an old key, and which release opens or migrates a backup made by an older release?

quotes:
The configuration holds exactly these items and no other: the store's
   location; the backup location and the backup key (A18); the owner
   credential; one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client
   Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel (R0-20, R0-23).

When the owner changes the key, older backups stay encrypted
   with the key they were made with; the owner keeps that key in the vault
   until the last of them is deleted (R0-23).

Right after writing a backup Registry checks it: it decrypts it into a
   temporary file in the backup location, opens it for reading only, checks
   that it is the store version of its release, that the store's own
   integrity check passes and that its audit log ends at the recorded
   sequence number, and removes the temporary file.

The store must open for reading and writing and carry
   the store version of the running release; a store of another version, or
   one that does not open, fails the start — bringing a store to a new version
   is a step of the release, not of the start.

Restoring production replaces the store with a backup, by the owner on the
   host while Registry is stopped (Explicit exclusions).
judgement.divergence: One restoration procedure temporarily configures the historical key and runs the release that made the backup before applying release migrations, while another expects the current release and current key to open the backup directly or refuses it; the owner and all callers notice whether restoration succeeds and which release can serve afterward.
judgement.why: The texts retain backups across key and release changes but leave open how an old key is supplied and how an older store version reaches a startable current release.

topics.topic: Security requirements for owner-session, CSRF, and confirmation values
questions: What entropy, generation and non-disclosure rules apply to the owner-session cookie value, CSRF value and pending confirmation value?
Must these values be cryptographically unpredictable, how long must they be, must comparison be constant-time, and may either appear in a URL or diagnostic?

quotes:
The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner
   session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over
   HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only
   to Registry's own origin.

Every change in the owner interface carries the CSRF protection bound to
   its session (R0-29); one from another session or none is refused.

An action that asks for confirmation (Identity formats) is submitted with a
   confirmation value Registry made when it showed the step: one-time, kept in
   the owner session, bound to the action, its target, the revision or access
   version the step showed, and its inputs — for the import, the file's digest
   and the picks.

Facts: its identity, minted by Registry at sign-in ("Identity formats");
written once: the instant it began, its expiry at the latest and its CSRF
value (R0-29); changed by the owner's requests (State 2 A13, A16; owner,
2026-10-31): the instant of its last request, which starts as the instant it
began; at most one pending confirmation — its one-time value, the action, its
target, the revision or access version and the inputs it is bound to, and
the instant it was shown — made when a confirmation step is shown, replaced
by the next one shown and cleared when used; and at most one uploaded import
file, replaced by the next upload and dropped when the import is accepted.
judgement.divergence: One implementation generates secret, cryptographically unpredictable session, CSRF and confirmation values and prevents their disclosure, while another uses predictable values or exposes them in diagnostics; an attacker and the owner notice whether unauthorized owner actions can be forged.
judgement.why: The texts define binding and lifetime but leave the security properties of the bearer and anti-forgery values to the implementer.

topics.topic: Whether Kernel end-session calls require and match an access version
questions: Must Cabinet Kernel's 'end an agent session' state and match the access version, or is the version required only when the owner ends it?
Must Kernel's end-session call state the access version, and is it refused as stale if a request or owner action changed the session meanwhile?

quotes:
Cabinet Kernel ends a session when its agent session ends; the owner may
   end any session in the owner interface.

Ending a session states the current version and removes the session with it (A11); it makes no next
   version.

The owner's actions on a session — granting, revoking, changing or clearing
   the active project, answering a request, ending the session — state the
   access version the owner saw; a stale one is refused and nothing changes.
judgement.divergence: One implementation requires Kernel's end-session call to state and match the current access version, while another applies the version precondition only to the owner's end action; Kernel and the owner notice whether a concurrent request or access change makes Kernel's end fail.
judgement.why: The general ending rule says a version is stated, but the stale-version rule expressly scopes its check to owner actions and does not settle Kernel's call.

topics.topic: Whether an accepted no-op audit erasure must append an erasure entry
questions: Does every accepted audit erasure create an erasure entry, or only one that actually removes entries?
Is the formal invariant conditional on at least one old entry being removed, or must every accepted erasure write an entry?

quotes:
An erasure that removes no entry changes nothing: it is accepted, writes no
   entry and mints no confirmation id (A14).

erase(d) accepted => no entry with instant < start_of(d) remains
                     and the erasure entry e has e.instant >= start_of(d)
judgement.why: The normative rule permits an accepted erasure with no new entry, while the unconditional formal invariant requires an erasure entry for every accepted erasure.

topics.topic: Whether ended agent-session identities may be reused without making audits ambiguous
questions: How can Registry preserve the claim that audit entries naming a session identity mean one session if that identity is registered again?
How can audit entries naming a session identity continue to mean one session when Registry accepts reuse of an ended identity as a new session?

quotes:
Cabinet Kernel names every agent session
   with an identity it never uses again, so an ended identity is never
   registered again and the audit entries naming it mean one session; Registry
   relies on this as it relies on Kernel naming the session (R0-53, R0-77).

A registration of an ended identity, Kernel's defect, makes a new session
   with an empty set.
judgement.why: The one-session meaning is explicitly guaranteed by Kernel's non-reuse obligation; reuse is classified as Kernel's defect and Registry nevertheless specifies that it creates a new empty session.

topics.topic: Whether imported child records may reference unpicked projects
questions: Must every imported room and pointer name the picked project whose import includes it, or is naming an unpicked but file-present project allowed?
Must every imported room and pointer name its picked parent project, or can a picked import bring a child whose named project is present only in the unpicked part of the file?

quotes:
Registry checks what the picks bring in — the picked projects with their
   rooms and pointers and the v1 values they name — and nothing else of the
   file: records only of projects the owner did not pick are neither checked,
   shown as conflicts nor imported, and take no part in the duplicate-id
   check.

A brought-in record is malformed when: a required value is missing (A02);
   it names a project or room the file does not hold; an id occurs
   twice among the file's records of one kind; a status is outside its
   vocabulary, or a pointer is `withdrawn` (v1 never withdrew one, M05); a
   pointer's type is not declared or its owner service is not the type's
   (A22); the versions of a project's pointers of one type are not 1..n, or
   more than one of them is `published`, or a `superseded` one is not lower
   than a later version; an instant cannot be read; an `active` project has an
   archived instant or an `archived` one has none; a `superseded` pointer has
   no superseded instant or a `published` one has one; a record was changed,
   archived or superseded before it was created, added or published.

An accepted import stores every picked project with its rooms and pointers,
   the Customers it makes, the migration closure (M10) and its one audit entry
   (M09) in one transaction.

A picked project whose room names a project absent from the file refuses
   the import as malformed.
judgement.divergence: One importer rejects or excludes a room or pointer whose named project is not among the picks, while another accepts it because that project exists elsewhere in the file; the owner notices whether confirmation succeeds and which child records are imported.
judgement.why: The texts exclude records belonging only to unpicked projects but test referential validity only against presence in the whole file, leaving cross-reference to a file-present unpicked project unresolved.

topics.topic: Accepted encoding and measurement of the configuration secret minimum length
questions: Against which representation is the 32-byte minimum measured, and which encodings are accepted?

topics.topic: Concurrency scenarios that must be covered by the security review
questions: Are concurrent confirmation submissions, audit erasure versus appends, import confirmations, owner-session mutations and backup/restore interactions intentionally outside the concurrency review, or must they be reviewed too?

topics.topic: Create-request replay semantics after erasure or anonymisation removes the request id
questions: After erasure, anonymisation or whole-project deletion removes the original request id, must a later call with that id remain a replay, be refused, or create a new record?

topics.topic: Disclosure classification and representation of personal data in pending confirmations
questions: What class applies to personal-data values copied into a pending confirmation: does the owner session inherit `personal_data`, or must it retain only a digest or other non-personal binding?

topics.topic: Disposition of other owner sessions' uploaded files after import completion
questions: If multiple owner sessions have uploaded files and one session successfully imports, are files held by the other sessions dropped immediately or retained until those sessions end or replace them?

topics.topic: Effect of backup-creation and deletion failures on retention
questions: Does failure of backup creation lengthen backup retention even when deletion succeeds, or does only deletion failure lengthen the erasure horizon?

topics.topic: Event at which a confirmation identifier is created
questions: Is a confirmation id minted when the confirmation step is shown, on every submitted confirmation, or only when a confirmed action is accepted and changes state?

topics.topic: Lifecycle and eligibility checks required for a repeated create request
questions: Which stage-6 lifecycle and eligibility checks apply to a create repeat?

topics.topic: Ordering agent-authority reads against access revocation and session changes
questions: At what event is an agent-authority read ordered against revocation, archiving or session end?

topics.topic: Ordering and deterministic resolution of concurrent mutations to one owner session
questions: How are simultaneous requests in one owner session ordered so last_request cannot move backward, only one confirmation submission can consume the value, and the winning upload or confirmation is deterministic?

topics.topic: Ordering audit erasure against concurrent audit-producing transactions
questions: How is audit erasure ordered against concurrent transactions that append entries, especially one that obtains an old instant before the erasure but commits afterward?

topics.topic: Outcome of concurrent valid import confirmations
questions: What is the required outcome when two valid import confirmations race?

topics.topic: Owner-session expiry and last-request timing during a request
questions: At what instant is validity decided and last_request advanced, and may a request accepted before a deadline commit after the session expires?

topics.topic: Permitted containment relationship between store and backup locations
questions: May the backup location equal, contain, or be contained by the store location?

topics.topic: Permitted storage and crash cleanup of uploaded personal-data import files
questions: May the personal-data import file be written to a temporary filesystem location, or must it remain memory-only, and how is crash cleanup guaranteed?

topics.topic: Project context used to authorize Kernel withdrawal without a project id
questions: For a Kernel withdrawal, is authorization checked against the pointer's project regardless of the active project, or is the active project used because the request names no project?

topics.topic: Required temporal relationships among imported record timestamps
questions: Which additional relationships among created, last-changed, archived, published and superseded instants must an import satisfy?

topics.topic: Restoring pre-migration backups while preserving permanent import closure
questions: May production restore a backup predating the successful migration, and if so how is the permanent one-import closure restored?

topics.topic: Whether a failed daily backup attempt consumes the day's run across restarts
questions: Does a failed attempt consume that day's single run, and how does Registry preserve that fact across a restart when no successful backup exists?

topics.topic: Whether a refused upload replaces an already-held valid import file
questions: Does a refused upload discard and replace the valid file already held in the owner session?

topics.topic: Whether audit sequence numbers lost by restoring an older backup may be reused
questions: May numbers assigned after the backup and lost by restoration be reused?

topics.topic: Which confirmation submissions consume the pending confirmation value
questions: After valid session and CSRF checks, does any confirmation submission consume the session's pending value, or only submission of that exact pending value?
